html:
The Irritila, called Laguneros by the Spanish, were hunter-gatherers of the Comarca Lagunera, the lake country on the border of Coahuila and Durango in northern Mexico. They lived around the shallow lakes fed by the Nazas and Aguanaval rivers, fishing and gathering desert plants.

Jesuit missionaries founded the mission of Parras among them in 1598. Epidemics, forced labour on Spanish estates and wars with Spanish settlers broke them up during the 1600s, and they disappear from the records by the 1700s. Little is known of their language. Their neighbours included the Tepehuán to the west and the Coahuiltecan peoples to the east.
